bias: Blank entries treated as missing, not zero
plain_language: DHIS2 can't tell "no data reported" from "zero deaths": both show up blank, so real reporting gaps end up hiding deaths.
About 1 in 5 births happen at home; their outcomes never enter facility data.
Tertiary hospitals often use both DHIS2 and their own electronic records, so deaths logged locally may not reach DHIS2.

bias: Private / faith-based hospitals not fully integrated
plain_language: These hospitals report 11-25% of deaths but are not fully connected to the national system.

bias: Denominator mismatch (live births vs admitted babies)
plain_language: Death rates can shift depending on whether the denominator counts all live births or only admitted newborns.
Without patient-level records, the smallest and sickest babies are hardest to track accurately.
